extraction.name: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images. The dataset covers a multitude of different document types including tables, forms, figures, and various textual, graphical and structural elements.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV] 5 Jan 2021
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand picked for use in the dataset. Majority of documents in the library are binarized. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages which only have running text. Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library. The final set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Documents are from 5 major industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical. Documents include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR tokens are extracted using a commercial OCR application. For BERT QA models, OCR tokens recognized on document images are serialized to a single string, separated by space, in top-left to bottom-right order. To approximate answer spans, the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string is found following an approach proposed in TriviaQA.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. In stage 2, a worker was shown an image and questions defined in the first stage (but not the answers), and was required to enter answers for the questions and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions if they found them inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity. In stage 3, if none of the answers from stage 1 matched exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review where questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it. The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers. Human performance measurement was done with help of volunteers from the authors' institution.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application for extracting OCR tokens
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken a toll on the image quality. The authors tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since they did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits. The train split has 39,463 questions and 10,194 images, the validation split has 5,349 questions and 1,286 images and the test split has 5,188 questions and 1,287 images. DocVQA is modelled as an extractive QA problem where answers are extracted verbatim from the document, similar to extractive QA tasks in NLP and VQA in case of ST-VQA.
